ranked.headline: Logical-gate architectures and mediator-assisted control push toward fault tolerance
ranked.summary: Lattice-surgery teleportation on superconducting qubits appears alongside proposals for color-code T gates, transversal ion gates and finite-blockade CCZ.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is engineering logical and entangling operations across hardware platforms. One experiment teleports logical qubits via lattice surgery on 41 superconducting qubits using distance-three surface-code patches. Proposals target other fault-tolerance bottlenecks. A persistent-mediator architecture reuses a 3D color-code block to apply repeated logical T gates to a 2D register. Parallel transversal CZ gates across double-well trapped-ion wells use dynamical decoupling and crosstalk mitigation. A reset-assisted scheme uses noisy mediator qubits to drive high-fidelity gates on long-lived data qubits. On neutral atoms, an analytically specified CCZ gate operates under finite Rydberg interactions and is compared with an antiblockade scheme. A separate analog Rydberg experiment performs phase estimation of energies and gaps for up to 19 atoms via Loschmidt echoes. Peripheral work covers Krotov control of GHZ-type XXZ states, bosonic Fock-state stabilization, an Fe2+:forsterite qubit, and Majorana reservoir computing.

ranked.headline: Exact samplers and simulators target noisy, near-Clifford and generative quantum circuits
ranked.summary: Several preprints push exact or hybrid sampling of noisy and near-Clifford QEC circuits, alongside work on certifying and training quantum samplers.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is classical machinery for sampling from noisy quantum circuits, especially for error-correction workloads. MASQ is an exact measurement-adaptive sampler for near-Clifford QEC circuits that materializes only measurement-relevant non-Clifford contributions. Compiled Clifford-augmented MPS accelerate coherent-noise QEC simulation, reaching distance-9 surface codes. Pre-trajectory sampling with batched GPU execution is extended to mid-circuit measurements and general Kraus channels. A second strand treats quantum devices as samplers. One preprint studies how physical qubit embeddings bias annealer sampling of the 2D Ising model and feeds QPU-learned proposals into corrected Monte Carlo. Another trains a hypernetwork that maps Hamiltonian parameters to circuit angles for ground-state samplers. A third finds the Fisher trace uninformative for certifying Born machines and shows that kernel-metric verdicts depend on tolerance. Peripheral items cover noisy Grover stopping thresholds, commutator-guided repair of shallow circuits, and Koopman-von Neumann flow simulation with surface-code resource estimates.

ranked.headline: Simulations calibrate assembly bias and nuisance systematics in cosmological inference
ranked.summary: New preprints use TNG, HR4 and HESTIA simulations to test assembly bias, n(z) and lens-multipole systematics relevant to Euclid and DESI analyses.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is using simulations to quantify systematics and secondary dependencies between observables and cosmological parameters. Two papers address nuisance modeling directly. On-the-fly Gaussian Process reconstruction of n(z) for Euclid-like 3×2pt analyses shows that redshift-distribution systematics can bias w0wa. IllustrisTNG ellipticals show that multipole mass terms bias time-delay H0 by 1–6%. Halo secondary bias is the second focus. In TNG300, the unbound matter fraction in the circum-halo medium largely accounts for secondary bias, through cold tidal and hot inertial accretion regimes. Luminosity-weighted marked correlations are proposed as a null test for galaxy assembly bias and validated on DESI-BGS mocks at 0.1<z<0.4. Direct simulation–observation comparisons include SDSS genus topology against HR4, where modern galaxy models match much better than earlier ones. Local Group satellite-pair statistics are compared against HESTIA and show an excess of close Milky Way pairs. More peripheral items cover a GR test using cluster clustering in the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys, Gini-index BCG dominance in SPT and Planck clusters, and Euclid Q1 radio-loud AGN fractions.

ranked.headline: Fast, accurate decoders and optimized syndrome circuits push qLDPC codes toward practice
ranked.summary: Several new decoders target microsecond-scale latency on qLDPC codes, alongside circuit-scheduling and code-design work aimed at lower logical error rates.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is decoding under real-time constraints, increasingly for qLDPC codes rather than only surface codes. SCOPE, a physics-informed parallel decoder, reports a logical error rate of 4.82e-10 on the [[144,12,12]] bivariate bicycle code with 173.8 ns latency. TEMPO-BP adapts per-variable memory strength via local feedback and lowers failure rates relative to BP+OSD and Relay-BP. TCBP-JOBS runs on GPUs, learns calibrated fault probabilities and matches Tesseract accuracy. A hybrid sliding-window decoder for trapped-ion noise uses soft-output confidence to switch windows and improves on BP-LSD. For surface codes, Beyond Blossom reports a 4.23x geometric-mean speedup for CPU MWPM via local predecoding. A second strand optimizes syndrome-extraction circuits: Proxima schedules them using a DEM-based proximity metric, and CP-SAT synthesis reduces logical error rates. Code-design work adds Armillary rate-1/2 codes for fixed-connectivity superconducting hardware and rate-optimal small color codes.

ranked.headline: Real-time decoders, FPGA control and hardware-aware compilers converge on fault tolerance
ranked.summary: Sub-microsecond FPGA decoders, Pauli frame tracking, and multi-GPU relay-BP decoding all target the real-time classical bottleneck in fault-tolerant QEC.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is co-design of the classical stack that must keep pace with quantum hardware, especially for error correction. On decoding, Rapids pairs a streaming neural decoder with FPGAs to decode surface-code syndromes in under a microsecond with lower logical error rates than existing decoders. Pêlagos scales relay belief-propagation across multiple GPUs. A survey frames hierarchical decoding and its latency trade-offs. CHEQ provides FPGA-based decoder evaluation via geometric-skip circuit-level noise sampling, matching Stim firing rates within 0.16%. QuFrame closes the QEC loop within 1 μs through real-time Pauli frame tracking. Platform-specific compilation forms a second strand. NEAT optimizes AOD transport for neutral atoms, and an FPGA quantum data processing unit cuts atom-assembly latency. QCCDCert offers Lean-verified QCCD co-design scaling to 512 qubits, and QWeaver handles MLIR-based circuit cutting. What is new is the treatment of latency bounds and hardware constraints as first-class design targets.

ranked.headline: Symmetry and structure exploited to cut cost in quantum simulation and state preparation
ranked.summary: New preprints enforce spin and charge symmetry and use sparse or structured methods, with hardware runs up to 96 qubits, to reduce simulation resources.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is exploiting symmetry or problem structure to reduce resources in quantum and classical simulation of many-body systems. Spin-adapted SqDRIFT completes sampled configurations to obtain exact S^2 eigenstates, and a loading circuit prepares U(1)×SU(2)-symmetric MPS with lower Toffoli cost for fault-tolerant algorithms. Sparse quantum prolate diagonalization applies compressed sensing to cut sample complexity from O(N_s) to O(log N_s), demonstrated on trapped ions. Gutzwiller embedding, RG-guided variational circuits on a 16-qubit IQM device, and quantum-walk search on complete bipartite graphs show structure-informed hardware use. Pauli propagation partitioned via F2-linear hashing reaches over 10^11 strings, and an effective Hamiltonian method models 96-transmon quench dynamics, supporting classical benchmarking and device characterization.

ranked.headline: Surface-code experiments and simulators target correlated noise, leakage, and calibration on superconducting hardware
ranked.summary: Eight November 2026 preprints pair superconducting-hardware error-correction demonstrations with noise-aware calibration, mitigation, simulation and resource-prediction tools.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is confronting realistic, non-ideal noise in error-correcting and error-mitigated quantum computation on superconducting devices. Experimental work scales surface-code stability tests to 7x7 patches on a 105-qubit processor and identifies temporally correlated heating-to-|3> leakage, while magic state cultivation is implemented with lattice-surgery escapes on IBM hardware. Supporting methods include syndrome-based recalibration via gate-error amplification (GEARS), logical-error prediction and geometry selection for rectangular surface codes under biased noise, and Ellis, a Pauli-frame simulator handling qubit loss and leakage. Complementary NISQ-oriented items extend bnZNE mitigation to randomized circuits and propose a noise-aware testing oracle with controlled false-positive rate. The common novelty is coupling characterization of noise structure to decoding, calibration, and resource choices.

ranked.headline: Compilers, formal proofs and certification tools target fault-tolerant quantum circuit design
ranked.summary: Eight preprints in one week pair quantum compilers with formal verification and exact code-distance certification across fault-tolerant workflows.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is software infrastructure for fault-tolerant quantum computing, in which compilation and correctness guarantees are developed together. Compilation work spans block-encoding synthesis from matrix formulas (MARBLE), latency-preserving rewrites of dynamic circuits with a Lean 4-verified validator (qlin), and routing for dual-rail cavity qubits (PRISM). Verification work includes a formally verified harness for Shor's order finding at O(n^(2+ε)) gate cost, QECLean for machine-verified code specification, and QEDist for exact stabilizer-code distance certification. Architecture-level papers formalize reaction depth, with constant-depth coherent Boolean arithmetic, and explore fault-tolerant state-preparation check constructions through Block Checks and Pareto tree search. What is new is the combination of resource optimization with machine-checkable or exact guarantees. The items do not all share the verification theme.

ranked.headline: Evolving dark energy confronted with DESI, CMB, and supernova data via parametric and reconstructed models
ranked.summary: Eight November 2026 preprints test dynamical dark energy against DESI, CMB and supernova data, with independent SN Ia datasets aimed at the w0-wa tension.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is testing departures from a cosmological constant using DESI BAO or full-shape data with CMB, supernovae and lensing. Model-level work compares one-parameter vacuum histories within VCDM, where F42 is favored by AIC with supernovae, and a full-shape DESI DR1 analysis finds the scalar-field Fading Dark Sector model outperforming CPL w0-wa. Two non-parametric reconstructions of dark-energy density and gravitational response report a phantom-divide crossing near z≈0.5–0.7, one also asking whether dark energy clusters. A generalised axion-like quintessence model is confronted with multiple probes. Complementary efforts target systematics: the LEMAITRE project and a ZTF/SNLS/HSC calibration proposal provide independent SN Ia constraints, while a 0i Einstein-equation proposal offers observable-only tests of dark-sector degeneracies.

ranked.headline: Symmetry, geometry and magnon responses proposed as probes and controls of unconventional magnetic order
ranked.summary: Eight preprints propose optical, spin-current, thermal Hall and magnonic responses that expose or control order in altermagnets, antiferromagnets and spin nematics.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is theoretical identification of responses that reveal or exploit hidden order in unconventional magnets. For altermagnets and noncoplanar antiferromagnets, octupolar magneto-optical effects offer field-free optical probes, while nonlinear spin generation and spin photocurrent are proposed as probes of spin-space symmetry, domains and quantum geometry. Twist engineering of collinear bilayers is proposed to give quasicrystalline altermagnets with high-order spin polarization. On the magnon side, single magnons and bound magnon pairs in pyrochlore spin-nematic magnets give competing Berry-curvature thermal Hall contributions and a field-tunable sign reversal. CrI3 nanotubes in an axial field acquire a conical phase and a large pseudo-orbital magnon moment, and gated domain boundaries in BiFeO3 modulate nonreciprocal magnons in a proposed transistor. Cavity photon condensation from scalar spin chirality and defect-activated orbital magnetoelectric responses are peripheral. All items are preprints.

ranked.headline: Forecasts and new statistics test LCDM and dark energy with 21-cm, CMB, lensing and PTA data
ranked.summary: Seven preprints from mid-November apply new summary statistics and forecasts to test LCDM, dark energy and new physics with upcoming 21-cm, CMB and timing data.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is stress-testing standard cosmology with forecasts and new statistics rather than new measurements. For 21-cm data, one preprint applies persistent homology to Cosmic Dawn brightness maps, another introduces a phase gradient spectrum for the squeezed bispectrum, and a third forecasts SKA1-Low sensitivity to boosted dark matter. Bayesian forecasts for Simons Observatory and CMB-S4 address whether dynamical dark energy can be separated from LCDM shadow models. The time-delay cosmography forecast finds that mass-sheet transformation uncertainties reduce the significance of the decreasing H0 trend to ~1σ. The binaryfog surrogate examines how astrophysical priors affect evidence for new-physics sources in pulsar timing arrays. The Shapley jet-alignment result is a separate observational large-scale-structure claim at 4.5σ.

ranked.headline: Compilers target hardware cost directly: pulse latency, routing, and two-qubit depth
ranked.summary: New preprints tie compilation to hardware cost metrics, reporting gains over Qiskit O3 and EPOC baselines and cutting QAOA two-qubit depth.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is compilation guided by hardware-level cost rather than abstract gate count. SCOPE uses an operator Schmidt time surrogate to reduce pulse execution latency and reports gains over EPOC on 104 benchmarks. The quspect SDK selects routings after coupling-constrained resynthesis, reaching 0.616x Qiskit O3 two-qubit gates on 55 circuits across five targets. For Max-Cut QAOA on non-native graphs, MinLA surrogates prune interactions to lower two-qubit depth, and classical configuration recovery follows. CAVQS adds variational synthesis with unitary redistribution and mid-circuit dynamic reconstruction. Adjacent items on speed limits, QSVT inversion degree, and quantum Hamiltonian descent are algorithmic or theoretical neighbors rather than compilation results.

ranked.headline: Fast, differentiable models and new probes extend cosmological inference beyond standard LSST-era pipelines
ranked.summary: Seven preprints from mid-November 2026 pair emulators and forward models for LSST-era analyses with FRB-based and DESI DR2 tests of cosmology and GR.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is modeling and inference infrastructure for upcoming survey analyses. Hi-COLA trains a Cubic Galileon emulator for the nonlinear matter power spectrum, validated for LSST Year 1. bihalofit-JAX provides a differentiable nonlinear bispectrum code with projected statistics, running orders of magnitude faster than existing approaches. A cubic-order EFT forward model for the Lyman-alpha forest, validated on CAMELS and Sherwood, supplies BAO shift predictions and simulation-based priors. A secondary thread uses alternative probes: a physics-informed neural network reconstructs dark energy and the growth index from DESI DR2 to test GR, while fast radio bursts map baryons with IllustrisTNG and yield a first Ωm–w constraint from 125 localized bursts alone. The QCD equation-of-state study on early-universe expansion and the stochastic gravitational-wave spectrum is more peripheral.

ranked.headline: Cosmology inference is being scaled with posterior reuse, GPU samplers, and ML for survey data
ranked.summary: Six November 2026 preprints target inference cost and robustness for GW, Euclid, LSST and SKA analyses, from posterior reuse to a 16-team EoR comparison.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is inference infrastructure for next-generation cosmological datasets. ASPIRE reuses existing posteriors for joint dark-siren cosmological and population inference, with 6-28x speedups over reanalysis. samsara++ implements trans-dimensional MCMC in C++/CUDA for LISA global fits with overlapping Galactic binaries and noise. The LSST DESC cluster pipeline is validated on cosmoDC2 mocks, constraining Omega_c and sigma_8 from cluster counts. On the machine-learning side, Euclid DR1 strong-lens detection depends strongly on training-set composition, image format and ensembling, and EuclidFM learns 128-dim embeddings from Q1 photometry. SKA SDC3b compares 16 teams' EoR pipelines and finds inter-team variability, which highlights methodological systematics. The items are heterogeneous in probe but share a focus on computational efficiency and validation.

ranked.headline: Optical and electrical pulses deterministically write and probe skyrmions and compensated magnetic states
ranked.summary: Six November 2026 preprints report ps optical skyrmion writing, low-Gd all-optical switching, and electrical or probe access to compensated order.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is deterministic control of magnetic textures and compensated order with ultrafast optical or electrical stimuli. Picosecond circularly polarized pulses write fixed-chirality Néel skyrmions in Co/Pt, with chirality set by the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction, and laser pulses imprint antiferromagnetic skyrmions in a coupled ferromagnetic/antiferromagnetic bilayer within picoseconds. Atomistic simulations find all-optical helicity-independent switching in GdCo with as little as 1.5 at.% Gd. Electrical writing and planar Hall readout of a compensated state in artificial spin ice extends control to spin-orbit torque. Pulsed-field MOKE on Fe2Mo3O8 and NV magnetometry of thermally activated switching in CrPS4 trilayers are probe-oriented studies connected more loosely, addressing metamagnetism and bistability in antiferromagnetic systems.

ranked.headline: Dark energy models and distance probes are tested against DESI BAO, CMB and supernova data
ranked.summary: Fresh DESI-era analyses test axion and scalar-field dark energy while new BAO and low-z supernova work extends the distance-ladder probes.
ranked.synthesis: Most items test dark energy beyond a fixed positive cosmological constant using current distance and growth data. One analysis constrains axion quintessence with a negative cosmological constant using DES, DESI BAO, CMB and growth data, finding no compelling evidence for a negative value. Another tests a single canonical scalar field with a double-power potential as both early and late dark energy against CMB, DESI BAO and Pantheon+, with the summary noting a raised H0. Complementary probe work reports a BAO measurement in an all-sky cluster catalog and the 2MASS Redshift Survey, consistent with DESI DR2, and proposes a Rubin twilight program for nearby Type Ia supernovae that improves the dark-energy figure of merit in simulations. The decihertz eccentric IMRI paper is a gravitational-wave template-bias study and is not part of this thread.

ranked.headline: Perturbative and halo-model cross-spectra for LSS tracers are tested against mock and lightcone simulations
ranked.summary: Five preprints from mid-November 2026 validate cross-correlation models on simulations, ahead of DESI Lyman-alpha and SPHEREx applications.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is checking theoretical models of tracer auto- and cross-spectra against simulations before data analysis. Two Lyman-alpha papers test EFT descriptions: a minimal tree-level EFT for 21 cm and Lyα spectra at z=2.4-4.2 that constrains HI and Lyα biases, and a full-shape power spectrum plus bispectrum analysis validated on AbacusSummit mocks at z=2.5 for DESI. The SPHEREx pair forecasts extragalactic background light cross-correlated with CMB lensing, with IGL detectable and emission lines reachable by fitting the continuum, and finds halo-model predictions matching lightcone simulations. A baryonification paper adds two methods for generating thermal SZ Compton-y maps from dark-matter-only lightcones. The new element is simulation-level validation across these tracers.

ranked.headline: Euclid DR1 calibration chains for NIR imaging, spectroscopy and ground-based photometry are documented
ranked.summary: Five Euclid DR1 papers released together document the calibration and processing chains that underpin the first data release.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is the instrument-level processing and calibration underlying Euclid DR1. The papers cover NISP near-infrared processing and data products, NIR astrometric calibration with distortion modelling, quality control and residuals against Gaia DR3 reaching 30 mas, and SIR spectroscopic calibration that models the focal plane globally to meet wavelength and flux requirements. Ground-based optical imaging over about 2500 deg2 supplies colours, with photometric stability and depth validated for photo-z and PSF calibration. An overarching paper reviews the calibration plan, its implementation and its performance against requirements, including corrections for flux, astrometry, PSF, shear and wavelength. The new element is the documented performance of these chains at DR1 scale; the items present pipelines and validation, not cosmological constraints.

ranked.headline: Tunable resonances in metasurfaces, nanoantennas and microresonators set optical response
ranked.summary: Five preprints report quantified resonance control across BIC metasurfaces, plasmonic antennas and coupled microresonators, spanning telecom to THz.
ranked.synthesis: The items share a focus on engineering resonances in subwavelength or microscale structures, with response set by material and geometry. A silicon BIC metasurface uses QBIC-GMR strong coupling to reach intrinsic circular dichroism of 0.995 with Q of 1083 at 1653.9 nm. In MAPbBr3 metasurfaces, BIC resonances are tuned reversibly and continuously by HCl/HBr vapor anion exchange. Coupled TiO2 and perovskite-coated microresonators show tunable whispering gallery mode hybridization. Plasmonic nanoantenna arrays with hollow-core fiber coupling give polarization-resilient THz operation, with 2.1 mW output and 145 dB dynamic range. A coaxial nanoantenna study maps inverse Faraday magnetization across Au, Ag, Cu, Al and TiN. Platforms and spectral ranges differ; the common advance is quantified, tunable resonance control.

ranked.headline: Computational correction and measurement design extend structured-light and indirect imaging
ranked.summary: Five preprints address turbulence, quantization, temporal mixing, memory limits and spectral speed in structured-light and computational imaging.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is recovering optical field information from constrained or imperfect measurements through computation or engineered illumination and readout. Active convolved illumination is reviewed as a way to preserve mode structure in turbulent media via segmented reciprocal-space control. Two single-pixel imaging papers treat measurement imperfections differently: a Fourier-domain response-matrix correction addresses quantization errors in binary-encoded Fourier acquisition, and a calibration and composite-readout framework turns temporal mixing into a measurement resource for real-time operation. A stochastic gradient descent framework for X-ray ptychography reduces peak GPU memory to 65% and time to 22% relative to the baseline. Event-camera Fourier-transform hyperspectral microscopy with continuous birefringent interferometer scanning reaches real-time widefield spectral acquisition. The items differ in modality; what is new is the targeted treatment of specific error sources or resource bottlenecks within each.

ranked.headline: Switchable order steers valley and exciton states in van der Waals layers
ranked.summary: Recent preprints use ferroelectric, magnetic and optical order in adjacent layers as switchable handles on valley and exciton properties in TMDs.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is external control of excitonic and valley properties in van der Waals systems through an adjacent or intrinsic ordered layer. WS2/CrSBr heterostructures show type-II band alignment, magnetic-proximity Zeeman valley splitting and spin-selective interlayer charge transfer. In WSe2/CrPS4, a light-controlled Néel vector switches valley polarization optically via spin-polarized charge transfer. In rhombohedral-stacked bilayer WSe2, sliding ferroelectricity yields hysteretic, electrically switchable exciton photoluminescence and Raman response, and in few-layer R-stacked WSe2 it switches dipolar exciton transport and drives dipole reconfiguration toward quadrupolar excitons. The NbOCl2 preprint reports room-temperature antiferroelectricity in 2D flakes with reversible switching to a ferroelectric state, probed by SHG, extending the switchable-order theme without addressing valley or exciton states directly. What is new is the range of switchable order parameters, magnetic, ferroelectric and optical, used as handles on valley and exciton states.

ranked.headline: Photonic lattices control flat bands, BIC merging, and mobility edges
ranked.summary: Recent preprints report experimental and model-based control of flat bands, bound states in the continuum, and edge states in engineered photonic structures.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of engineered photonic lattices to control the localization and confinement of optical modes, namely flat bands, bound states in the continuum (BICs), and mobility edges. Two preprints are model-based: a four-mode non-Hermitian model of C2-symmetric photonic-crystal slabs in which coupling sign governs BIC merging, with reported Q scaling as k^-6 and flatband formation, and a one-dimensional non-Hermitian pseudospin lattice in which non-Hermiticity can embed compact localized states in a continuum. A third preprint reports an experimental demonstration of exact mobility edges and flat-band states in a two-dimensional photonic quasicrystal, using auxiliary subsystems and photonic waveguides. A fourth preprint proposes antihelical gapless edge states in a spin-polarized Dirac semimetal realized as a photonic metacrystal with staggered bianisotropy; it addresses edge states rather than flat bands. What is new is the explicit tuning of flat-band and BIC physics through coupling sign and non-Hermiticity, together with experimental verification of exact mobility edges in a photonic quasicrystal.

ranked.headline: Chern and Z2 invariants read from zeros of wavefunctions and overlaps
ranked.summary: Four preprints recast topological invariants as readable from zeros, overlaps, and localizers rather than the bulk Hamiltonian alone.
ranked.synthesis: The four preprints share a dominant thread: topological invariants and boundary-protected modes are diagnosed through quantities other than the conventional bulk Hamiltonian spectrum. Arxiv 2611.25037 reads relative Chern and Z2 invariants of two gapped band structures from zeros of the occupied-subspace overlap determinant. Arxiv 2611.25028 shows that crystalline symmetry can enforce wavefunction zeros and vorticities characterizing Chern topology, readable from band-dispersion shifts. Arxiv 2611.26160 generalizes the spectral localizer to unify Z and Z2 invariants across hinge modes, Dirac nodes, and valley boundary modes. Arxiv 2611.19328 argues that edge modes of the non-Hermitian Loschmidt matrix, rather than Hamiltonian topology, protect boundary effects in dynamical quantum phase transitions. What is new is the shift of the diagnostic object to overlap and wavefunction zeros, localizer operators, and non-Hermitian Loschmidt matrices. The DQPT item is the least direct fit to this thread, since it concerns dynamics rather than ground-state band topology.

ranked.headline: Disorder reshapes Chern, orbital Hall, and Weyl magnetotransport beyond clean limits
ranked.summary: Recent preprints move transport modeling of Chern, orbital Hall, and Weyl systems beyond clean-limit and constant-relaxation-time treatments.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is that transport in topological and orbital-active systems is being recast with explicit disorder rather than clean-limit or constant-relaxation-time descriptions. In twisted bilayer MoTe2, layer-dependent disorder is reported to shape the widths and transitions of integer and fractional Chern plateaus. A Kubo-Bastin Chebyshev study of a centrosymmetric sp3 square lattice examines whether the quadrupole-origin orbital Hall effect survives disorder and how it can be tuned. For multi-Weyl semimetals, a generalized semiclassical Boltzmann treatment beyond constant relaxation time incorporates orbital moment and intervalley scattering, with monopole charge N as a parameter. The newest item extends the picture: structural and electrostatic disorder, including in amorphous graphene, is reported to generate sizable orbital Hall currents absent in pristine systems. Together these works treat disorder as a source of transport response rather than a perturbation to be neglected.

ranked.headline: Non-sinusoidal Josephson junctions are being engineered as qubit and qutrit elements
ranked.summary: Qubit platforms increasingly exploit departures from the ideal sinusoidal current-phase relation of Josephson junctions.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is treating Josephson junction transport as a design variable rather than assuming an ideal sinusoidal current-phase relation. The qutrit proposal exploits the second harmonic of the current-phase relation in three-junction loops, with altermagnetic elements. The Al/AlOx/Al tunnel-junction study examines non-ergodic area scaling of Andreev transport against the ideal sinusoidal assumption. Gatemon work reports in-situ ternary InAsSb/Al nanowire junctions with GHz-scale gate tunability and coherent control, with T1 of about 0.2-1 us. The Ge quantum well study finds gate-tunable spin splitting for Andreev spin qubits that is independent of junction width, unlike InAs. What is new is the set of materials platforms and deliberate departures from conventional junction behavior, though the studies differ in maturity and scope.

ranked.headline: Exact solvability exposes exceptional points and fragmentation in lattice models
ranked.summary: Non-Hermitian and hyperbolic extensions of Kitaev-type models are now treated with exact or analytically controlled methods.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is exact or analytically controlled analysis of lattice models whose spectra or localization properties depart from standard Hermitian, translation-invariant expectations. An exactly solvable non-Hermitian Kitaev chain with unequal pairing amplitudes exhibits an exceptional point where many-body energies collapse, accompanied by Lifshitz criticality. Non-Hermitian fermionic chains with random imaginary gauge fields show erratic skin localization and density fragmentation into Fermi domains. A disordered spin-1 chain admits an exact binary-tree Fock-space structure that rigorously bounds spreading at strong disorder. The three-colored Kitaev model is examined on finite hyperbolic periodic-boundary clusters through ground-state flux sectors and two-vison gaps. What is new is the pairing of exact solvability with diagnostics of exceptional spectra, fragmentation, and localization across non-Hermitian, disordered, and hyperbolic-geometry settings.

ranked.headline: Spectral selectivity shapes thermal radiation absorption and emission across wavelength
ranked.summary: Recent preprints model wavelength-selective emitters and absorbers for thermophotovoltaic and solar-thermal conversion without experimental validation yet.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is spectral control of thermal radiation: tailoring how a surface absorbs, emits, and reflects across wavelength to govern energy conversion. A 16-layer MgO/Si multilayer on tungsten is inverse-designed as a selective emitter for GaSb thermophotovoltaic cells, with modeled conversion of 47.0%. A gold-carbon metasurface uses a dielectric spacer to tune gap-mode overlap with carbon, sharpening infrared roll-off in solar-thermal absorption. The SpaderOptics database provides optical and thermal-radiative properties of 21 materials under the AM0 solar spectrum, offering property data relevant to absorber and emitter design. The photonic Maxwell's demon proposal is more distant from this thread, using one-way dielectric mirrors and wavelength-converting materials in a 3D box to accumulate blackbody radiation. All four items are numerical or proposal-stage, and none reports experimental validation.

ranked.headline: Accidental BICs in photonic lattices and metasurfaces tied to parity and nonlocality
ranked.summary: Recent preprints connect accidental bound states in the continuum to radiation-source parity and spatial nonlocality in open photonic systems.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is the characterization of bound states in the continuum (BICs), localized modes that persist within the radiation continuum of open photonic systems. Two items address accidental BICs directly: one shows that in vertically asymmetric photonic lattices they are governed by radiation-source parity and recovered through radiation-source parity restoration, while the other models metasurface BICs as converging reflection and transmission zeros and argues that accidental BICs require spatially nonlocal response. A third study examines Berry phase and topological quasi-bound states in Möbius resonators, reporting that the phase depends on mode. A fourth item reports hybrid graphene plasmon-silica phonon eigenmodes in a graphene ring, forming quadrupolar modes and multiband vortex states. The new element across the set is the framing of accidental BIC existence in terms of parity and nonlocality.

ranked.headline: Engineered nonreciprocity and modulation in compact photonic and sheet-based platforms
ranked.summary: Compact integrated and sheet-based platforms now probe nonreciprocal and modulated optical response beyond static, reciprocal limits.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is controlling optical response beyond static, reciprocal, linear behavior in compact geometries. A computational study proposes integrated optical isolators built from nonreciprocal 2D semiconductors that exploit spin-momentum locking, including an all-optical isolator concept. A separate study reports asymmetric frequency conversion in temporally modulated Floquet metasurfaces formed from three closely spaced conducting sheets, presented as violating Kirchhoff's law of thermal radiation. An experimental tripartite van der Waals cavity magnonic device reports hierarchical anti-crossing, reduced magnon loss, and a tunable coupled-mode Hamiltonian. A theoretical inverse-design study of transparent conducting oxide cavities at the epsilon-near-zero point reports stronger light confinement and faster dynamics. What is new is the engineering of nonreciprocity, modulation, and coupling in compact platforms. The items differ in method and maturity, and they do not share a single mechanism.

ranked.headline: Monolayer MoSe2 attenuates spintronic THz emission about fourfold
ranked.summary: Interfacial layers now set spin, charge, and optical response across organic, molecular, and two-dimensional spintronic platforms.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the role of an interface between a functional layer and an adjacent organic, molecular, or two-dimensional layer in governing transport and optical response. In NDI-based organic spin valves with Co/Au or graphene/Co/Au electrodes, in situ thermal annealing degrades magnetoresistance. Monolayer MoSe2 covering Py/Au or Py/Pt spintronic terahertz emitters attenuates the emitted amplitude about fourfold, attributed to absorption by free carriers. Optical spectroscopy of non-planar spin-crossover molecules on monolayer transition-metal dichalcogenides shows efficient interlayer coupling via Forster energy transfer. The new element is the use of a monolayer TMD as an active overlayer that modulates spintronic terahertz emission, alongside evidence of efficient molecule-TMD interlayer coupling. The organic spin valve study does not share the same spectroscopic or terahertz setting, so the link is interfacial rather than mechanistic.

ranked.headline: Surrogate and differentiable models accelerate photonic chip and waveguide design
ranked.summary: Open-source and surrogate-based tools are now reducing simulation cost in silicon and nitride photonic device design.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the replacement or streamlining of expensive full-physics simulation with purpose-built computational workflows for integrated photonic design. TARANG provides an open-source Python pipeline that takes refractive indices through to GDSII masks for silicon nitride microcomb chips, with validated dispersion. A neural network surrogate trained on double-pulse femtosecond simulations predicts optothermal observables for thin silicon films on fused silica, enabling fast design exploration. A differentiable coupled-mode-theory surrogate supports gradient-based inverse design of multimode waveguides, reducing transmission error by 17-37% relative to forward EME on TFLN. The new element across these works is the use of surrogate or end-to-end differentiable models to make design loops faster and more tractable, although the three address distinct materials platforms and physical regimes.

ranked.headline: Multi-stage optimization defines full-skyrmionic polarimetry for optical skyrmions
ranked.summary: Three recent preprints apply structured-light and ultrafast techniques to measure optical skyrmions and high-dimensional biphoton states.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the precise characterization of structured optical degrees of freedom. The leading item defines full-skyrmionic polarimetry and a multi-stage optimization framework that uses topological evaluating functions to measure optical skyrmions accurately. A second preprint analytically computes the full Laguerre-Gaussian spectrum of SPDC biphotons with a generating-function method, enabling efficient evaluation of high-dimensional states. A third simulates backward-scattering photoelectron holography in polar CO driven by sub-cycle laser pulses, separating forward and backward scattering fringes. The items are heterogeneous: the third concerns molecular strong-field dynamics rather than light-state metrology. What is new is the explicit focus on complete rather than partial characterization, as signaled by the word full in two titles.
